content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge issued an UNDERDETERMINED verdict and grounded it on the internal character of a single verse, which is exactly the practice the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse.", "room": "I weighed the judge's clause \"immediately qualified\" under two readings: first, that the judge is describing Luke 2:48-49 as one verse carrying both Mary's \"thy father\" and the child's \"my Father's business\", i.e., a verse admitting both readings, and using that balance as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which K-S2 forbids; second, that the clause merely endorses the defender's chain answer in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4 as defeating the challenge, in which case the proper label would be STANDS and the verse's balance would be no ground at all -- the label UNDERDETERMINED is coherent only under the first reading, so I took it as the operative one.", "why": "The judge rested an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on one verse's internal balance -- Mary's \"thy father\" set against the child's \"my Father's business\" -- which is precisely a verse that admits both readings, and K-S2 says such a verse's non-statement is never a ground for UNDERDETERMINED."}
